summary: Detach 88/58 from the house-near-palace quotation and attach it to the added bath-rental example.
rationale: The supplied verse rents a bath for a month from its owner, not a house near a government palace. Keep prs 10/28 with the original quotation.

data.turoyo: Azzən, maṭən li walay d Šat w Benʕat. Yatu b baxča, makrele i baxča mu ǧenenči, nošo lo ṭore d ʕobər yawma li baxča.
data.translation: So reisten sie und gelangten in die Stadt Schât-u-Ben'ât. In einem Baumgarten liessen sie sich nieder und mieteten denselben vom Gärtner, indem sie ihm auftrugen, er solle an diesem Tage keinen Menschen in den Garten hineinlassen.

rationale: Thin III.1 Preterit cell; an explicitly m-marked lessor and a rented garden.

data.turoyo: Hano, u=faqqa ste azzé, mən səmle? Makrele u=ḥəmmam ʕal yarḥo me more d u=ḥəmmam.
data.translation: Der Schulmeister nun ging, was tat er? Er mietete ein Bad für einen Monat von dem Besitzer des Bades.

rationale: Correct full context for the inherited secondary reference 88/58: a rented bath, one-month term and me-marked lessor.

data.turoyo: Zox l bayn i walay, kraylox bayto w itaw buwe xəd d ḥuzena.
data.translation: Geh in die Stadt, miete dir ein Haus und wohne darin, bis wir sehen, wie die Sache sich gestaltet

rationale: Unusual vowel-less Imperativ kraylox beside inherited akray-lox; same instruction, quoted only to retain the attested spelling.

summary: All accepted verbal uses belong to rental homonym kry 2, III.1, not shortening kry 1. Rented objects are zero-marked; garden and bath sources are m-/me-marked lessors.
The bath at 88/58 has ʕal yarḥo for a one-month rental term. This is a duration phrase, not a recipient or the rented object.
Imperativ kraylox has a beneficiary suffix coreferential with the addressee; initial vowel variation against inherited akray-lox is retained, without rewriting the inherited example.
l təkriyo in 2/114 expresses rental availability and matches the inherited Infinitiv example. The source/entry vowel difference does not justify another box or a new rent-out sense.
The flagged 88/247 translation is not quoted. Turoyo confirms rental, but the German additionally narrates an event absent from that verse.
Compare Lahdo Traitor 1/46 makralle with the recording: is it hire, or a liquid variant of kly III stop? The edition’s stopped cannot establish a new sense by itself.
Verify markeli at 20/17 against makreli: authentic metathesis or source error?
Align 88/247 with the surrounding edition before using its translation; the supplied German includes later head-smashing absent from the assigned Turoyo.
Verify PrS 4/7 versus inherited prs 10/28 numbering, and the vowel variation təkriyo/tukriyo at 2/114.

rationale: Morgen is a noun in am Morgen and is capitalized in the supplied corpus translation.
This is a verbal infinitive in zu vermieten sei, not a nominalized infinitive. The corpus translation also has zu vermieten sei.

summary: Rented objects include houses, rooms, flats, a garden, taxis, a pickup and a bath; no new sense follows from object type.
